extracted.intended_audience: authors, reviewers, editors and readers of Nature Communications (potential contributors and reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Policy describing Nature Communications' trial of publishing peer review histories for papers submitted from January 2016, including what is published, consent procedures, exclusions, and evaluation plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to publish peer review history
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of papers submitted from January 2016 will be given the option to publish the peer review history of their paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a trial, the journal will be publishing all reviewer comments to authors and author rebuttal letters for published papers submitted from January 2016, unless the authors ask us not to. Upon acceptance of a paper, authors will be asked whether they agree to the publication of the peer review file along with the accepted version of the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author opt-out (consent) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication of the peer review file is subject to the authors' consent; authors can ask that the peer review not be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors will be asked upon acceptance whether they agree to publication of the peer review file; the trial's success will be evaluated by monitoring parameters such as author opt-out rates and a report is planned within a year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limited to Nature Communications reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Published peer review files will only contain the peer review history at Nature Communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a manuscript is submitted to us after review at another Nature journal, those referee reports and author rebuttal letters will remain confidential, as those reports were submitted without prior consent to be published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer identity disclosure only with explicit reviewer consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review identities will only be released if a reviewer explicitly agrees to this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, a reviewer can agree to be identified by signing the comments made to the authors with their name; apart from such circumstances, reviewer anonymity will be honoured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents to be published: reviewer comments and author responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Published peer review files will focus on the comments of the reviewers and the authors' responses to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The files will contain reviewer comments to authors and the authors' rebuttal/response letters, providing transparency about the information that led to publication decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of confidential correspondence and internal editorial material
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence between authors and editors, reviewer comments only to the editors, and internal discussions between editors will remain confidential and will not be published in the peer review files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exclusion is intended to strike a balance between making decision-related information available and enabling reviewers, authors and editors to communicate frankly and privately where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial additions when peer review files are incomplete
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial comments may be added to the peer review document in cases where not all of the circumstances that led to an editorial decision on a manuscript are fully captured in peer review files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may add explanatory commentary to ensure readers understand the decision context; the ultimate decision to publish remains with the editors and is taken after careful consideration of all arguments raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal: increase openness and credit reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: The policy aims to open up editorial decision-making, contribute to scientific appreciation of papers, and provide more credit to reviewers by making their assessments reach a larger audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By enabling publication of reviewer reports and authors' responses, the journal hopes to enhance understanding and accessibility of published papers and recognise reviewers' work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with open access and licensing policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The move to publish peer review files coincides with the journal's transformation to full open access and publication under a Creative Commons licence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From January all new papers will be published with a Creative Commons open access licence, and subscription-based archive content will be made free to read and available for non-commercial text and data mining; peer review files will be made available alongside accepted manuscripts as part of this openness initiative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial evaluation metrics (monitoring)
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal will evaluate the success of the transparent peer review trial by monitoring parameters such as author opt-out rates and will provide a report within a year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring opt-out rates and other parameters will inform whether the policy is successful and guide future decisions about continuing or modifying the practice.
